note: Independent re-audit against RFC 6396 Section 4.4.2 ("Only one BGP message SHALL be encoded in the BGP4MP_MESSAGE Subtype.") in its complete-message and transparent-content context. Re-read all three tagged tests (TestOneBGPMessagePerBGP4MPRecord, TestRFC6396WireCaptureIgnoresSemanticSynthesis, TestRFC6396WireMessagesNeverCoalesce) and current producers (OnBGPMessage, WriteBGP4MPMessage, observeReceivedWire, observedBGPWriter.observe and selected_refresh_eor.go::complete). The only change in the tagged test unit TestRFC6396WireCaptureIgnoresSemanticSynthesis is the added unused leading _ *Session parameter on the s.onMessageReceived callback signature; all inputs, semantic synthesis/reset checks, and exact single-record byte-for-byte MRT assertions are unchanged. OnBGPMessage's new 2-byte/4-byte AS subtype selection (4db24861ee) shares the single WriteBGP4MPMessage framing path for both AS widths, writing exactly one observed BGP message per MRT record; observedBGPWriter.observe -> complete still forwards each individual complete frame once after read-only EOR detection. TestOneBGPMessagePerBGP4MPRecord (3 distinct messages -> 3 byte-identical records), TestRFC6396WireCaptureIgnoresSemanticSynthesis (1 wire UPDATE -> 1 record despite 2 synthetic TAW callbacks or reset), and TestRFC6396WireMessagesNeverCoalesce (2 unequal wire UPDATEs -> 2 byte-identical records despite 1 coalesced semantic body) would all fail on batching, splitting, or reconstruction. The {single-polarity: positive} producer-cardinality annotation remains justified. Verdict: enforced.
